extracted.subtask_description: A set of journalism transparency standards (the Trust Project Indicators) intended to be displayed on news articles to help assess and communicate quality, sourcing, and production practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by The Trust Project as one of its Trust Indicators (named on the RAND summary page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAND summary provides no detailed element-level description here; generally presented as an indicator news organizations will display on their articles. The Trust Project aims to increase transparency in journalism and to amplify high-quality journalism to fight disinformation. The tool is content- and process-focused, human-implemented (not automated), and has partnerships with Google, Facebook, and Bing; funding includes Craig Newmark, Democracy Fund, Knight Foundation, Markkula Foundation. RAND is not affiliated with The Trust Project and this RAND page was not updated after Dec 2020.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed description included on this RAND summary. See overall project purpose and metadata in guidance for Best Practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Scope (increase transparency / fight disinformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Project is a collaborative initiative developing standards (Trust Indicators) to increase transparency in journalism; indicators are intended to be displayed on news organizations' articles to help users identify higher-quality journalism and avoid lower-quality sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAND notes the project was founded in 2016 and that the Trust Project Indicators are content- and process-focused. The initiative is human-implemented (not automated), has tech partners (Google, Facebook, Bing), and received funding from several foundations and donors. RAND is not affiliated with The Trust Project and this RAND page was selected for RAND's database because it fit researchers' inclusion criteria; the RAND summary had not been updated after December 2020. No external evaluations were found on the RAND page.
